The memory address is generated by treating the block index and the intra-block offset separately, then combining them.
The coordinates are divided by the block size $B=32$.
The integer quotients form the block index.
The lower 5 bits of each coordinate ($X_{4\dots0}, Y_{4\dots0}, Z_{4\dots0}$) are interleaved to form the intra-block offset.
Here, $X_{n \dots 5}$ denotes the bits of $X$ from bit $n$ down to bit 5.
This avoids iterative bit-shifting for the lower portion.

The 32-entry table mentioned in the source is an optimization for this bitwise operation, likely precomputing the result for small values or facilitating parallel processing, but the logical result is the bit-interleaved offset.*

The memory layout itself does not change the total storage size of the volume.
